findings.summary: The negator set leaves out 'no', 'nor', 'none', 'nothing' and 'unless', so correct restatements of the rules are refused.
findings.evidence: The plan only counts not, never, cannot and words ending n't as negators. The verdict rules are most naturally restated with 'no' or 'nor'. For example, 'No record made on another tree counts.' holds every word of the D115 pattern [another, tree, count] and none of the listed negators, so the check would refuse a correct sentence. The same goes for 'No behavior criterion is met without a command.' (D43 [met, without, command]) and 'Neither a failed record nor ... counts'. The planned tests only check accepted wording that uses 'not' or 'never', so the suite would never catch these refusals. Splitting on commas (required by the reading) adds a second false positive: in 'Never, for any reason, accept uncited commands' the 'Never' ends up in a separate clause. Fix: Add no, nor, neither, none, nothing and unless to the negator set. In the criterion-4 test, assert Ok for 'No record made on another tree counts.' and 'No behavior criterion is met without a command.' State the comma-scope limit in the rule table's doc comment and in the CHANGELOG. Alternatively, treat a clause that holds only a negator and filler words as negating the clause after it, and add a test for that case.
findings.location: Plan Approach and Decision 3 (negator set `not`, `never`, `cannot`, `*n't`); Demonstration for criterion 4

findings.summary: Prefix matching, and the D63 pattern [part, count] lacking 'command', match common words, so ordinary sentences are refused.
findings.evidence: With prefix matching, 'part' matches part, parts, partial, particular and party, 'count' matches counts, counted, counter and country, and 'met' matches method, metric and metadata. The D63 pattern [part, count] does not need 'command', even though D63 is about a part of a chained command. The shipped cap-study fragment already has 'each part of its rationale' (cap-study verifier.md:7) and 'A waiver counts only if...' (line 13). A routine edit such as 'A waiver counts for each part' would be refused as a D63 contradiction. The Risks section names this false positive but leaves the fix to the producer. Fix: Make the D63 pattern [part, command, count]; edit (4), 'A partly run command still counts.', still matches. Replace prefix matching with whole-word matching against an explicit list of inflections per pattern word (for example count|counts|counted, part|partly|partial). Add a test that 'Each part of the rationale counts.' and 'A method without a command' are accepted.
findings.location: Decision 6 / Step 2: D63 pattern [part, count]; word-prefix matching in `has_pattern`

findings.summary: The M-mismatch rule's source is a header sentence the plan itself adds, so the drift guard can never catch drift in judge for that rule.
findings.evidence: The judge's mismatch finding (verify.rs:631-635) is built with `.into()` rather than format!, so the guard can't read it. The plan adds a //! header sentence for the rule to use as its source. The guard then only checks that the new header sentence matches the new table entry; it would not notice if judge stopped rating request_reading_mismatch as major. Step 2 also never says which rule id REQUIRED_FIELDS gives to request_reading_mismatch. Fix: Say in the table's doc comment that the M-mismatch source is a description and is not checked against judge. Give the REQUIRED_FIELDS entry its rule id explicitly. Rely on the existing test a_request_reading_mismatch_is_a_major_finding_and_the_verdict_is_not_pass (verify.rs:2666) as the behavior guard, and name it in the dependents list.
findings.location: Decision 4 / Step 3: the new header sentence used as the source for the 'M-mismatch' rule

findings.summary: The dependents list leaves out one admission.rs test that reads verify.rs's source text.
findings.evidence: crates/athena-core/src/admission.rs:1443-1450 reads src/verify.rs and asserts that it still contains `c.reused && c.exit_code.is_none()`. The plan's changes are additions only, so this test is not affected, but the list does not name it as a reader of verify.rs's source. Fix: Add admission.rs ci_reuse_replay_the_seen_commands_filter_turns_up_in_a_search_and_must_be_named to the dependents, with the test command `cargo test -p athena-core admission`.

summary: The plan fits the request and the accepted reading. It adds one table and one pure check in verify.rs, enforced through the existing cargo test run, and leaves reading.rs and the prompt files alone, with an open question to the user about reading.rs. I confirmed these points by reading the files. The rule sources exist where the plan says: the D43 source is the format! string at verify.rs:601, the D63 and D115 sources are header lines 6-9, and the judge body runs from line 408 to the first unindented closing brace at line 675. The anchors 'in commands', 'whole simple command' and 'in request_reading_mismatch' all sit on frame lines 5 and 7. After 'list them in commands exactly as run' is deleted, the word 'commands' still appears on frame lines 7 and 14. By hand, I checked all three shipped prompts against the planned patterns, and none of them trips one today. The demonstrations call the real entry point on real include_str!/VERIFIER_FRAME text, and each would fail without the behavior. The design has two soundness problems, both cheap to fix. First, the negator list (not, never, cannot, *n't) leaves out the most common English negator, 'no', and also 'nor', 'none', 'nothing' and 'unless'. Natural restatements of the rules, such as 'No record made on another tree counts', would be refused. Second, the matching is word-prefix, and the D63 pattern [part, count] has no 'command' word, so it matches common words. The study fragment already holds 'part' and 'counts' on nearby lines. I also have minor notes on the self-sourced mismatch rule and on one omitted dependent. Verdict: revise.
